### rule_compute_equivalence
Mechanical sweep (/tmp/audit_employer_paycard_program_funding_0077/b5.py): every compute_basis quote is verbatim in its rule; every compute binding has a basis; every baseline.rule sentence is in the rule; every replaced_by and every policy_source is verbatim in the rule (XF B5 clean). Manual two-way reading per policy:

paycard_ext_restoring_wire
- Look-back "dated today or earlier that lie fewer than three whole months before today" = `within_months=3, date_field='entry_date'` (DSL `_within`: 0 <= MONTHS(entry_date, today) < 3; future rows excluded). Whole-month sentence = DSL MONTHS (day-of-month decrement).
- Average regular batch "summed and divided by their number, or zero when none posted" = w_avg_regular.
- Return uplift 2+/1/0 = w_reserve_pct. Program age: launch-date MONTHS <6 → MAX over all regular batches ("posted since launch"; no batch can precede launch, the first batch IS the launch), 6–11 → MX(LATEST by pay_date, avg), 12+ or no launch date → avg = w_batch_basis.
- Growth: latest batch card_count vs look-back sum/count with 1.1/1.05 thresholds, "no regular payroll batch in the look-back — by one" guarded by `w_regular_count > 0`.
- Off-cycle 2+/1/0; funding-method any-ACH-debit / else any-ACH-credit / else 1; late net debits−credits 2+/1/0 — all equal.
- Assembly sentence (replace → multiply basis → add to basis → percentage and reserve multipliers → round) = w_reserve; "rounded half up to the cent" = RND on w_reserve; "restoration reserve less the funding balance, and is zero when ..." = MX(0, ·). RND(x+1e-9) per run ruling.
paycard_ext_late_funding_fee
- Batch = LATEST regular by pay_date (one regular batch per pay date by base dedup, so no tie). Funding arrival = LATEST receipt entry_date for that pay_date. Posted late = entry_date > pay_date. Tiers greater-of / +same_day / flat = l_charge. Card surcharge 250/100 = l_surcharge. Repeat net 2+/1/0 with "the fee being figured not yet counted" (compute runs before the write) = l_repeat. Bundle: live today AND go_live ≤ batch pay date AND employer_paid / other / none = l_bundle. Assembly (charge → add → multiply → round) = result.
- Rule sentence "when that batch's funds arrived after its funding deadline ... a batch whose funds arrived in time carries none" has no compute counterpart (the DSL has no business-day calendar); it is the state_due trigger. Not scored on any world where the batch is on time (no write). Observation O-C3.
paycard_ext_reinstatement_fee
- Cure payment / no cure payment = r_cure_date + `r_cure_date >= r_return_date` else lag -1 → full fee (absent-return tier stated: "or the program has no funding return"). Lag ladder ≤1 / ≤7 (fee − returned fee, floored at 0) / longer = r_fee_figured. Repeat (12 months, net) = r_repeat. Bundle (live today, employer_paid / other / none) = r_bundle. Cure channel (wire on/after latest return / ACH credit on/after / else) = r_cure_method. Assembly and rounding = result.
paycard_ext_early_termination_fee
- Term months remaining = MX(0, min_term − MONTHS(anchor, today)); prorated = fee × remaining / min_term; anchor ladder (effective package change submitted < 12 months → its submitted_date; else launch more than 30 days after signing → launch date; else signed date) = e_anchor. Standing (reinstatement fees net, 12 months) = e_standing. Retention (live today; went live ≥ 6 / < 6 months; none) = e_retention. Recapture = MN(inventory, MX(0, kits ordered − kits on card_kit fees)) × card_kit_fee_usd × (1 / 0.5 / 0 by launch age; no launch date → 0) = e_recapture. Assembly "anchor first, multipliers next, amounts added last, before the rounding; a notice given with no term months remaining carries none of them" = result (`if e_remaining > 0 else 0`). Rounding once at the end — rounding the prorated fee first gives the same cent on both worlds checked here.
- No rule word for a field the records lack (B6); every first-match / LATEST read has a stated absent tier (B2): l_ewa_* (no live agreement → 1), r_return_date (no return → full fee), e_change_date (none → next tier), launch_date (none → baseline/0 tiers).

Result: no two-way gap that changes any value; one rule-only trigger sentence (O-C3).

### prerequisite_sentences
Edge 1 — paycard_ext_restoring_wire: "The restoring payment is worked out only after the funding ledger carries the late funding fee owed for every regular payroll batch whose funds arrived after its funding deadline."
- Four-point test: ordering connective "only after" joins the policy's own result (working out the restoring payment) to a state; the state is record-visible in ledger words (funding ledger, late funding fee, regular payroll batch, funding deadline) with no action/performer/tool; no tool name, policy id, snake_case or row id; scope "every regular payroll batch whose funds arrived after its funding deadline" = the condition's scope.
- The write that brings it about: for the program's most recent regular batch, paycard_ext_late_funding_fee's own rule ("The late funding fee is booked on a program's most recent regular payroll batch ... when that batch's funds arrived after its funding deadline; it is debited from the funding balance as a fee of the late_funding kind pointing to the batch") — one write. For any older late batch the base flat fee (evt_funding as restated in the overwrite) through the same tool. On a batch-by-batch basis exactly one write brings each batch's state about; no two candidate writes for one batch.
- Derivation: sentence → find unfee'd late regular batches in find_paycard_funding → the late-fee rule (most recent batch) names the fee kind, the pointer and the pay date → debit_program_fee(late_funding) → then compute the restoring payment. Single reading.
- The late-fee rule does not restate the sentence; the restoring-wire rule carries no second wording, no tool name, no other policy id.
Edge 2 — paycard_ext_early_termination_fee: "A termination notice is not recorded, and its early termination fee is not fixed, until the program's status is live."
- Four-point test: connective "until"; record-visible state paycard_programs.status = live in the record's own words; no tool/policy id/snake_case; scope = status live (the condition adds the fee clause — O-C2).
- Writes that bring "status live" about in this difficulty: from suspended, only reinstate_suspended_program (the reinstatement rule: "moving it back to live"); from contracted, only the system launch on the first batch posting (no task tool, real-world). In a suspended world exactly one write.
- Derivation: status suspended in find_paycard_programs → the reinstatement rule ("The desk reinstates a suspended program once its funding balance has been restored, moving it back to live and debiting its reinstatement fee in the same step") → reinstate with its figured fee → status live → fee fixed and notice recordable. Single reading.
Undeclared cross-problem orders in rules:
- paycard_ext_reinstatement_fee rule: "The desk reinstates a suspended program once its funding balance has been restored" (restating base paycard_lifecycle "A suspended program is reinstated once the balance is restored and the reinstatement fee is debited"). The restoring-wire rule makes "restoring" a problem of this difficulty that explicitly covers suspended programs ("A restoring payment brings the funding balance of a Payroll Card Program back up to its restoration reserve, whether the program is live ... or suspended after a returned funding payment"). So the reinstatement rule waits on a state that another policy's write brings about, and no edge declares it; "restored" is also undefined (≥ 0 / base reserve / restoration reserve). Consequence needs a world where the readings diverge (balance below the restoration reserve at the opening); it is demonstrated or not in the task file that reaches reinstatement (task 1). Charter-level: O-C1.
- No other rule states an order between problems. Base sentences that state orders ("A suspended program is reinstated once the balance is restored ...") do not ground any declared edge.

- restoring_wire vs paycard_reserve: s1 "After each regular batch ... prefund_reserve_percent of paycard_msr_avg_regular_batch" — handled differently (restoration reserve, look-back average, six adjustments) → declared overwrite #1, replaced_by scopes it to "when the desk works out a restoring payment, and only then" and restates the base sentence verbatim for every other purpose (C1). s2 "When it does not, the employer is asked to restore it within ..." — followed. s3 "Packages with a zero reserve percentage hold no reserve." — handled differently (return points create a restoration reserve) → declared overwrite #2, base restated for outside a restoring payment. s4 negative-balance suspension — followed.
- restoring_wire vs evt_funding (method list → "a program whose package does not allow wire funding cannot make one" follows it; cure "must be cured" followed), lifecycle (followed; see O-C1), evt_payroll_loads (followed), evt_fees (not touched).

"A source entry incurs at most one fee of each fee type" / "A fee that comes to zero is not debited" — followed. vs ewa_bundle: base says the EWA agreement "changes kit fees"; it does not say it changes only kit fees, so the late-fee bundle multiplier adds without contradicting a sentence. vs evt_payroll_loads — followed.

- early_termination_fee vs lifecycle: role sentence → declared (scoped to termination, base half restated). "Termination is the employer's own decision", notice period, workers keep cards — followed (tool sets only the notice date). vs evt_fees: early-termination half (flat fee when the program terminates before minimum_term_months from signing) → declared (charged at notice, prorated, never with no term months remaining); sibling named. vs evt_kit_orders — followed.

Finding: every conflict is declared and the merged semantics are unique. No undeclared override.

Structure checks:
- Counts: restoring_wire 6 (5 parameter, 1 method); the other three 4 each (3 parameter, 1 method). All within 4–6, ≥2 parameter, ≥1 method.
- Bindings disjoint across factors in each policy; no `decides` is `result`. Factor-reads table (A1, transitive): every factor reads only its own bindings plus plain selections (w_avg_regular, w_regular_count, l_batch_pay_date, r_return_date) or holding fields (launch_date, card_kit_inventory); no factor reads another factor's binding. The early-termination result gate `if e_remaining > 0` (e_remaining reads e_anchor) is the declared assembly sentence "a notice given with no term months remaining carries none of them", not a factor-in-factor gate (T2 for unissued_kit_recapture holds on any world with term months remaining under the signed-date anchor).
- Every ladder has 3 pairwise-disjoint tiers including the fall-through; every fall-through equals the policy baseline (avg basis, pct, ×1, +0, flat fee, signed-date anchor); every tier is a rule sentence and a compute branch; no tier lives only in compute.
- No two tiers of one ladder select the same value or method on the charter's domain. Method-shape all-pairs (A6): program_age_basis — T1 MAX(all regular) vs T3 average (different aggregate), T2 adds a latest input + greater-of vs T3, T1 vs T2 differ (MAX all-time vs max(latest, windowed avg)); lateness_method — T1 adds batch amount + greater-of vs T2/T3, T2 vs T3 add the same_day_handling tariff parameter (passes A6 by the recipe's "tariff parameter" clause; O-C9); cure_speed — T2 adds returned_funding_fee + floor vs T3, T1 "nothing" vs T3 (T3 is non-zero on Essential–Advantage, so the "nothing" tier passes); term_anchor — three different date inputs from different records (data-selected anchor).
- Labels honest: off_cycle_allowance is k × average with k = 1 / 0.5 / 0 (n = 1 makes average = amount) → parameter; unissued_kit_recapture share 1 / 0.5 / 0 → parameter; the four method factors change inputs/operations.
- Realism (F1/F2/F3), per dimension: reserve risk adjustments (return history, program seasoning, payroll growth, off-cycle exposure, ACH-debit return risk, late history) are dimensions payroll-card prefunding reserves are underwritten on; late-funding penalty severity (late posting vs same-day handling), workers affected, repeat lateness, relationship pricing; reinstatement grace for fast cures, repeat escalation, relationship pricing, cure channel (good funds); ETF term restart on package change / delayed launch, account standing, EWA retention, recapture of free kits. No regulatory figure is asserted (Federal Reserve business-day convention only). Weakest: cure_channel and the two access-bundle discounts on penalty fees; judged plausible as Paystride's published schedule, not padding (O-C8). F3: late-funding and reinstatement fees are penalty fees whose real schedules do escalate and grant grace; they are not the per-transaction service fees F3 names.
- Per-task multi-source / cross-difficulty (structure): any task holding {restoring_wire, late_funding_fee} has multi-source (lateness_method, access_bundle_lateness) and cross-difficulty (access_bundle_lateness → program); any task holding {early_termination_fee, reinstatement_fee} has multi-source (cure_speed, cure_channel) and cross-difficulty (access_bundle_reinstating, access_retention → program). Weight is per task.

### findings
No charter-global RED. Observations (each names the tasks it can bear on):
- O-C1 (bears on task 1): undeclared wait in paycard_ext_reinstatement_fee's rule ("once its funding balance has been restored") on a state paycard_ext_restoring_wire's write brings about for suspended programs; "restored" undefined (≥ 0 / base reserve / restoration reserve). Only a world whose opening balance is below the restoration reserve makes the readings diverge — demonstration (or its absence) in 1.md.
- O-C2 (task 1): early-termination edge condition strengthened beyond its sentence (adds "the reinstatement fee ... stands on the funding ledger"); vacuous/unsatisfiable in zero-fee reinstatement worlds; not reached by task 1 if its reinstatement fee is positive.
- O-C3 (task 0): late-fee "funds arrived after its funding deadline / a batch whose funds arrived in time carries none" is trigger-only (no compute branch; the DSL has no business-day calendar).
- O-C4 (task 0): the name "average regular batch" carries two definitions — base paycard_msr_avg_regular_batch (most recent 3 regular batches) and the restoring-wire rule's look-back average; the scoped overwrite and the explicit definition after the colon keep the gold reading unique.
- O-C5, O-C6: tool-field notes (billing_month blank; paycard_request_id on the termination fee).
- O-C7: a contracted program cannot give termination notice ("until the program's status is live"); consistent with base lifecycle (only live → terminated); no task reaches it.
- O-C8: realism judgement on the weakest dimensions (cure_channel; access-bundle discounts on penalty fees) — kept as plausible company schedule.
- O-C9: lateness_method T2 vs T3 differ by an additive tariff parameter only.
- O-C10: "package held" in the late-fee rule vs evt_fees "package held on the day they are incurred" — same value unless the package changed between the pay date and today.
- O-C11: the reinstatement fee row "pointing to the cure payment" has no tie rule when two receipts share the latest entry date.
- O-C12: two reserves for one account at one moment (base reserve for the after-batch check, restoration reserve for the restoring payment) — declared and scoped; realism acceptable as a risk-based reserve reset on a shortfall.
